question: Is the Live Context Accumulator (handoff journal + rolling summary) actually firing at turn-end?
verdict: NOT RUNNING — wired Stop hook is a stale copy that lacks the accumulator

wiredHook.note: only appendTurn present is the unrelated Wave-65 session-context bridge (session-context.js), NOT handoff-journal.js

syncedRouterCopy.note: this is the correct accumulator-enabled copy, but it is NOT the one settings.json wires

postFixProof.method: manually invoked the (now-synced) wired hook with a real Stop payload (session_id + transcript_path + cwd)
postFixProof.note: git:{head,branch} present in the journal entry — exactly what host-extra.sessionGitFromJournal reads for the per-session honest branch/SHA

rootCause: settings.json Stop hook points at ~/.claude/hooks/gsd-turn-end.js (last updated 2026-06-14, before the accumulator existed). /mooter-update's glob syncs ~/.claude/tools/router/*.js but NOT the ~/.claude/hooks/ mirror, so the wired Stop hook never gained accumulateHandoff(). 63 sessions ran; 0 journals were ever written.
decision: FIX = sync the accumulator-enabled router copy over the stale hooks copy (harness-only, ~/.claude/, backup kept as gsd-turn-end.js.bak). The router copy requires handoff-journal.js/handoff-rollup.js by ABSOLUTE ROUTER_DIR, so it works unchanged from the hooks/ location. After the fix, the next turn-end writes <sid>.jsonl + (throttled) <sid>.summary.txt to ~/.claude/tools/router/handoff/, which host-extra.js already reads.
mooterUpdateGap: DOCUMENTED: /mooter-update does not mirror ~/.claude/hooks/. Until that glob is extended, hooks/gsd-turn-end.js must be re-synced manually after any turn-end change.
